subject.title: fix(codex): restore native PreToolUse relay delivery

question: Should OpenClaw accept the scoped policy-active Codex unified-exec and fresh-thread behavior before the patched Codex runtime is the default, or should this wait behind a fail-closed/broader mitigation path?
rationale: The code repair is mechanical, but the permanent behavior chooses a security boundary and upgrade-compatibility tradeoff for policy-active Codex users that automation cannot authorize.

options.title: Repair then review scoped positive delivery
options.body: Normalize `code_mode_exec` to `exec`, refresh conflicts, and then let maintainers decide whether the positive-delivery path is the preferred security boundary once the Codex runtime prerequisite is acceptable.

options.title: Prefer fail-closed until Codex ships the prerequisite
options.body: Keep this PR draft and use the fail-closed direction if maintainers want policy-active turns to abort rather than depend on patched positive hook delivery.

options.title: Adopt the broader native-surface mitigation
options.body: Use the broader disable-native-surfaces approach if maintainers decide unified exec positive delivery is not enough to cover every executable Codex-owned surface.

recommendation.title: Repair then review scoped positive delivery
recommendation.body: Normalize `code_mode_exec` to `exec`, refresh conflicts, and then let maintainers decide whether the positive-delivery path is the preferred security boundary once the Codex runtime prerequisite is acceptable.
